CLAIMS TO ATTACK (each PASS | FAIL | UNKNOWN with evidence):
AM1. Settled requirements: S-01 to S-33 and P-01 to P-07 are carried verbatim from their cited sources, none weakened, contradicted, or missing; D-01, D-02, D-05, and D-06 are settled correctly from the operator's instructions with the sources named; D-04, D-07, D-08, and D-09 record the operator's answers faithfully and are applied everywhere they bear (D-07 in section 20.4 and both TODOs; D-08 in section 12 and every time-bearing identifier; D-09 in section 19.3, both TODOs, and the store, where those existing records are unchanged); D-03 is correctly left with the operator.
AM2. Definitions and consistency: every unit of work is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler and one complete activity diagram (nested diagrams directly after their use); every policy, process, shared component (each defined once, DRY), entity, DTO, route and alias, MCP tool, client method, REPL verb, Director command, plugin verb, and error code is defined once and stated identically everywhere, including every list of a component's users and a unit's callers; sequences cover every externally callable request and every response; use cases cover UC-HV-01 to UC-HV-12; Addendum B shows the relationships; namespaces say where a thing goes and names say what it is.
AM3. Durability: crash windows W-01 to W-12 each recover as stated; invariants I-01 to I-13 hold and are proved by named acceptance criteria; leases, fences, the atomic finalization, the transactional outbox, and at-least-once execution are sound, and nothing claims exactly-once; every outcome of every internal unit (including stale_fence, audit_unavailable, evidence_corrupt, and a cancel found at close) has a stated next step for its caller; no two rules deadlock or loop (for example P-02's absence of a time limit against process cleanup, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC011, or a probe failure against an automatic re-probe).
AM4. Live output (S-22, P8): the design delivers each reviewer line while the reviewer runs, including a single line followed by silence, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC001 and AC003 discriminate it.
AM5. Audit and retention (S-29, I-13): every HV write has its ledger rows, an audit failure is a hard stop, every evidence read is recorded, evidence is retained until an explicit removal, and the audit ledger is append-only and never purged.
AM6. Reviewer facts: VI-01 to VI-08 and section 16.3 match the probe receipts and the installed CLIs (read their --help and versions; launch no review or probe of another agent).
AM7. Foundation amendments A-01 to A-12: each names the clause it replaces, the replacement is consistent with the foundation at 36783b79 (SHA-256 claimed in the amendment's first paragraph) and with the HV design, and together they are exactly the clauses that assume a manual HV with one configured grader.
AM8. Requirements: the 63 records and 21 mappings exist in the store and equal section 19.1 field by field (title, description, every acceptance criterion's id and text); all 133 acceptance criteria name a test; every mapping edge is backed by a TEST statement; section 19.4 binds every criterion to exactly one phase of section 20.1 in which everything it depends on exists, and distinguishes the H1 adapter and harness tests from the server-launched and live-check cases; the existing records of section 19.3 are named accurately.
AM9. Problems: P1 to P15 each match the cited source lines, receipts, and store records at this branch (P1 against the store's FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4; P11 and P15 against FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-005 criteria 2 and 1 and the hook's citations); REMED-HVPIPELINE-001 equals section 21; section 20.4's assignment of P1 to P15 to the plan's phases (D-07 for P10 to P15) is phase-consistent, each fix follows its owning plan's approved design, and each has a named test; for P10 to P15, the six findings match the Codex review of pull request 81 (posted after the merge), and the stated contradictions of two Codex remedies with approved decisions (the federation plan's D5; the foundation's FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005, created by that plan, not yet in the store) are accurate; the HostileReview worker of section 16.7 serves the stored FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 and -003 without changing them (R-25).
AM10. Plan holistically: PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001 derives from section 20 without contradiction or extension, including the H6 before H5 order and the round 1 record; the BDPv4 order (requirements, interfaces and stubs, TDD with mocks and a green mock gate, then implementation by bounded context) is kept; status NOT APPROVED, code freeze, and the HV of the plan's own work by the operator-named reviewer are stated; nothing instructs code before approval.
AM11. Process rulings: GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are no gate, requirement, or evidence; every build and test runs through Nuke; Octopus only for releases; every designed script or tool is PowerShell (no Node, bash, bats, or Python); integration and live checks run on a separate temporary instance, never the live server.
AM12. Hygiene: SPDX header; no en or em dash and no table in the amendment; no secret in the amendment, the commits under review, the receipts committed by the implementer, or the two TODOs; each commit of this effort is signed per the marker's Commit Signing rule; every push was a normal push with no force: the server audit docs/receipts/hv/20261017T110027-amendment1.push-audit.json covers every push up to caaa41b0, and `gh api "repos/sharpninja/McpServer/activity?ref=refs%2Fheads%2Fdocs%2Fhv-architecture-amendment-20261016&per_page=100"` (read only) shows each later push and its activity_type.
AM13. Round 1 closure: each of F01 to F21, U01, and U02 is resolved in the current text, store, TODOs, and receipts as its round 1 entry required (PASS), or is not (FAIL with what remains), and no fix contradicts another statement or an earlier accepted rule.
